definitions.explanation: A rank in the Japanese police force, below inspector (警部) and above sergeant (巡査部長). Roughly equivalent to a police sergeant or detective in English-speaking countries.

examples.japanese: {田中|たなか}{警部補|けいぶほ}が{事件|じけん}を{担当|たんとう}している。
examples.english: Assistant Inspector Tanaka is in charge of the case.

examples.japanese: {昇進|しょうしん}して{警部補|けいぶほ}になった。
examples.english: I was promoted to assistant inspector.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{刑事|けいじ}ドラマでは、{警部補|けいぶほ}が{主人公|しゅじんこう}を{務|つと}めることが{多|おお}く、{現場|げんば}で{捜査|そうさ}する{姿|すがた}がよく{描|えが}かれる。
examples.english: In Japanese detective dramas, assistant inspectors often serve as the protagonist, and they are frequently depicted investigating at the scene.

notes:
A compound of {警部|けいぶ} (police inspector) and {補|ほ} (assistant, deputy). This is one of the most frequently encountered police ranks in Japanese crime fiction and television dramas.

The Japanese police rank hierarchy from bottom to top: {巡査|じゅんさ} → {巡査部長|じゅんさぶちょう} → {警部補|けいぶほ} → {警部|けいぶ} → {警視|けいし} → {警視正|けいしせい}. The {警部補|けいぶほ} rank is notable because it is the highest rank that can be reached through promotion from the rank-and-file path.

JAPANESE POLICE RANKS:
- {巡査|じゅんさ}: police officer (lowest rank)
- {巡査部長|じゅんさぶちょう}: sergeant
- {警部補|けいぶほ}: assistant inspector
- {警部|けいぶ}: inspector
- {警視|けいし}: superintendent

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {警部|けいぶ}: police inspector — one rank above
- {刑事|けいじ}: detective — a job title rather than a rank; detectives are typically {巡査部長|じゅんさぶちょう} or {警部補|けいぶほ} rank
- {巡査|じゅんさ}: police officer — the entry-level rank
